subject: technology
unit_title: Web, App, and Accessible Interface Design
essential_question: How can understanding web, app, and accessible interface design help us explain, decide, create, or solve something that matters?
learning_objectives: Demonstrate current mastery of user testing through selected-response, constructed-response, and applied evidence.
Use subject-appropriate evidence or representation to communicate understanding of user testing.
Check, revise, or improve work about user testing using stated success criteria.
lesson_success_criteria: The learner completes the central task about user testing.
The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer.
The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
materials: unit-specific source, model, manipulatives, safe materials, or approved digital tool
task_brief: Day 5 of "Web, App, and Accessible Interface Design" (unit 3, grade 8) is a mastery demonstration on user testing. It is one step inside the unit — not the whole unit project — and takes about 40–60 minutes. The unit is working toward: Create an accessible multi-screen prototype or small site and document user-test changes. Today's work contributes to that by handling user testing at the mastery check stage, against the unit's wider topics of semantic structure, layout and responsive design, forms and validation without private data, and accessibility standards. This session produces graded evidence of record and must be completed independently.
primary_task: Demonstrate user testing independently, with no scaffold, prompts, or worked example in view. Produce a complete correct solution to a new problem, then prove it works: state the expected result first, run or hand-trace at least two cases including one boundary case, and show actual against expected. Then explain the reasoning in your own words well enough that a reader who has not seen user testing could follow why each decision was made. Both the working result and the explanation are required — either one alone is incomplete. The activity_setup block below supplies the complete central input, exact specification, execution method, test cases, debugging target, and equal-credit manual simulation; use those exact materials rather than waiting for another handout, account, service, or tool. Anchor today's work inside its unit: this session's evidence is about user testing, and it belongs to "Web, App, and Accessible Interface Design", which also covers separate topics such as semantic structure. Close out with this check before you stop: Rate confidence in user testing, cite one piece of evidence from today, and choose: ready to extend, ready to review later, or need a different explanation. At grade 8 the bar is independent work that anticipates the obvious objection: name the case most likely to break your result, test it, and report what happened.
requirements: Meet this lesson's own success criteria: The learner completes the central task about user testing., The learner gives evidence, reasoning, a model, or a documented process rather than an unsupported answer., and The learner checks or revises the work and can identify a next step.
Address the lesson objective: Demonstrate current mastery of user testing through selected-response, constructed-response, and applied evidence.
Produce the deliverable for a mastery demonstration: Independent complete solution, a two-case verification with expected against actual, and a self-contained written explanation.
Show the process, not only the result — a trace, test log, draft trail, or commit history.
Complete the check criteria list in this package before submitting.
deliverable: Independent complete solution, a two-case verification with expected against actual, and a self-contained written explanation.

central_input.title: Inline design brief for user testing
central_input.purpose: Design only for the fictional learner described here; no interview, public post, account, camera, or outside tester is needed.
central_input.fictional_user: Kai uses a keyboard, sometimes enlarges text to 200%, and wants a three-step way to track completed reading sessions without entering a name or location.
required_features: Add one reading session in at most three actions.
Show completion using both a word and a visual mark, not color alone.
Store only a fictional book label and a completed/not-completed value.
central_input.fixed_constraint: The prototype is a labelled paper sketch or local file; it is never published and collects no real personal data.

expected_behavior_and_specification: The response must apply user testing to at least three labelled details from the supplied central input.
Every conclusion must identify the exact row, card, requirement, or scenario sentence that supports it.
The response must include one concrete revision or decision and explain the check that would show whether it worked.
The response must name one limitation or trade-off and explain why the available evidence does not settle it.

execution_method.primary: Paper-first method: copy the short labels, annotate them, and complete the response in a notebook or any notes app. No download, installation, account, or internet access is needed.
execution_method.local_optional: A locally available word processor, spreadsheet, drawing tool, or slide editor may be used, but no particular brand or paid feature is required.
execution_method.check_path: Use the numbered specification and the package test/check criteria as a checklist; a parent or tutor can verify the cited labels without needing subject software.

test_cases.expected: one stated check with an observable pass condition
one limitation, unknown, or trade-off stated without inventing facts

debugging_target.observed_failure: An unsupported answer names the lesson topic but cites no labelled detail and has no observable way to check the proposed change.
debugging_target.target: Replace unsupported claims with evidence-linked claims, then add one pass/fail check for the proposed revision or decision.
debugging_target.passing_change: The exact accepted evidence map is intentionally withheld from learner material and is available only in the restricted trusted-adult scoring authority after the learner submits complete evidence.

equal_credit_alternative.method: A handwritten, typed, spoken-to-a-scribe, or labelled-diagram response earns identical credit when it addresses the same specification.
steps: Label three facts from the central input.
Explain how each fact connects to user testing.
State one revision or decision and its observable pass condition.
Name one limitation or missing fact without searching for outside information.
equal_credit_alternative.evidence_to_submit: Three labelled evidence links, the revision or decision, the pass condition, and the limitation or missing fact.

learner_experience.sequence_policy: Concept teaching, the analogous model, and guided practice precede protected independent evidence. Protected and fresh resolutions are absent from learner material and remain adult-only.
learning_targets: Demonstrate current mastery of user testing through selected-response, constructed-response, and applied evidence.
Use subject-appropriate evidence or representation to communicate understanding of user testing.
Check, revise, or improve work about user testing using stated success criteria.
Explain the evidence chain used to make or evaluate a result about user testing.
Transfer the reasoning to a fresh case without a completed target response in view.

concept_teaching.title: Design claims need observable access checks: user testing
concept_teaching.entry_check: Before reading, write one prediction about user testing and one observation that could show the prediction is wrong. This readiness record is no-penalty evidence.
explanation: user testing is treated here as a relationship among a specification, inspectable evidence, and a justified decision. A result is not secure merely because it looks plausible: the learner must state what should be true, identify evidence that bears on it, and explain why the evidence supports the claim.

Move from a labelled user need to a design choice, then to an observable access check; preference alone is not evidence. This keeps observation separate from interpretation and prevents a preferred answer from being rewritten as evidence after the fact.

Verification begins before execution or review. Record an expected result or pass condition, include a normal and boundary or stress case, compare actual with expected, and interpret every mismatch. After revision, rerun the complete relevant set so a local fix does not hide a regression elsewhere.

Correctness and quality require a limitation statement. Name what the supplied case, trace, dataset, or prototype cannot establish, then describe the additional evidence that would settle that point. For creation work, also name a viable alternative and the concrete clarity, access, time, storage, privacy, or reliability trade-off.

key_terms.definition: A goal or barrier grounded in a supplied user situation.
A limit the design must respect.
A cue that helps a person understand what action is possible.
An observable test of whether a person can perceive, understand, navigate, or operate the design.

application_check: Can you explain design claims need observable access checks in your own words using a new fictional example?
Did you write expected behavior or a pass condition before running, tracing, or judging the result?
Can another reader trace each conclusion to a state row, printed fact, requirement, or observation?
Did you name a boundary, stress case, missing fact, or limitation instead of assuming it away?

worked_example.title: Worked analogue: a readable two-action weather card
worked_example.complete_analogue_case: Fictional user Rowan uses only a keyboard and enlarges text to 200%. A paper weather card has icon-only controls and puts status in pale color alone.

annotations.reasoning: Need: Rowan must identify status and activate both controls without a pointer.
Evidence: the supplied card has no text status and no stated keyboard order.
Revision: add a status word beside the visual mark, label both controls, and number the focus order.
Check: at 200% size, a reader can name the status and reach both controls in the numbered order without color or dragging.
Limitation: a paper trace predicts access but does not replace later assistive-technology testing.

worked_example.completed_model: Need: Rowan must identify status and activate both controls without a pointer. Evidence: the supplied card has no text status and no stated keyboard order. Revision: add a status word beside the visual mark, label both controls, and number the focus order. Check: at 200% size, a reader can name the status and reach both controls in the numbered order without color or dragging. Limitation: a paper trace predicts access but does not replace later assistive-technology testing.
worked_example.transfer_prompt: Use the same evidence discipline on the protected task, but make a new decision from its different printed labels. Do not copy this model as the protected response.
worked_example.difference_from_protected_task: The worked model uses a different fictional setting, facts, labels, decision, and check. None of its completed claims answers the protected central input.

guided_task.title: Guided practice: claim → printed evidence → check
guided_task.alternate_case: A separate fictional practice card about user testing contains labels P1, P2, and P3. P1 states the intended purpose, P2 states a constraint, and P3 records an observed mismatch. It is not the protected case titled "Inline design brief for user testing."
prompts: Restate P1 as a criterion without adding facts.
Use P2 to reject one tempting but invalid response.
Use P3 to propose a revision and write an observable pass condition.
Name one conclusion the three labels cannot support.
guided_task.immediate_check: A complete guided response has one claim about user testing, the exact supporting label, one check, and one limitation.
guided_task.support_fade: The guided card names the purpose/constraint/mismatch roles. In protected work, the learner must locate those roles independently in the supplied central input; the fresh check offers only term or instruction clarification.

independent_task.title: Independent analysis/design: user testing
specification: The response must apply user testing to at least three labelled details from the supplied central input.
Every conclusion must identify the exact row, card, requirement, or scenario sentence that supports it.
The response must include one concrete revision or decision and explain the check that would show whether it worked.
The response must name one limitation or trade-off and explain why the available evidence does not settle it.
public_checks: the complete supplied central input → three or more evidence-linked observations
the proposed revision or decision → one stated check with an observable pass condition
the strongest competing interpretation → one limitation, unknown, or trade-off stated without inventing facts
evidence_requirements: At least three claims, each linked to an exact printed row, card, requirement, or scenario detail.
One feasible learner-authored revision, design, or decision made only from the supplied fictional case.
An observable pass condition written before judging the revision or decision.
One limitation, missing fact, or trade-off stated without inventing evidence.
A before/after or claim/check record showing how evidence changed the work.
independent_task.support: TERM_OR_INSTRUCTION_CLARIFICATION; one location/evidence cue may identify where to inspect but may not select the decision or give the resolution.

debugging_reasoning.title: Use the six-move evidence cycle
required_moves: Symptom: record expected versus actual without explaining it away.
Hypothesis: state one falsifiable cause about the claim or design state before revising.
Inspection: identify the first trace row or printed detail that bears on the hypothesis.
Predicted effect: state what one controlled change should alter and what it should leave unchanged.
Test and interpretation: compare actual with the prediction and mark the hypothesis supported, rejected, or not fully tested.
Verification: rerun all relevant checks and record any new limitation or next hypothesis.
debugging_reasoning.anti_guessing_rule: A working final artifact without a pre-change hypothesis and inspectable evidence is incomplete debugging/revision evidence.

remediation_routes.learner_signal: My conclusion names the topic but does not connect to exact printed evidence.
remediation_routes.title: Different representation: evidence cards and arrows
remediation_routes.alternate_teaching: Copy each printed fact onto a separate card. Draw an arrow from a fact to a claim only when the fact would make that claim more or less credible. Unconnected claims must be revised or removed.
remediation_routes.analogue_task: Use four new cards about a fictional library sign to build a fact → claim → check map for user testing; do not use the protected case.
remediation_routes.return_check: Complete the fresh mastery check with teaching materials closed. The original protected solution remains withheld.

remediation_routes.learner_signal: I changed or chose something before recording the mismatch and a testable reason.
remediation_routes.title: Different routine: the six-box evidence ladder
remediation_routes.alternate_teaching: Use six boxes in order: expected/actual, first divergence or decisive detail, hypothesis, predicted effect, one revision, rerun interpretation. Do not enter the revision box until the first four constrain what the change is meant to test.
remediation_routes.analogue_task: Apply the six boxes to a separate fictional clock-card mismatch related to user testing. Stop after the prediction, explain what result would reject the hypothesis, then finish the check.
remediation_routes.return_check: Complete the fresh mastery check independently. A correct but low-confidence response receives confirmation tied to evidence, not automatic reteaching.

fresh_mastery_check.title: Fresh transfer: Northstar card for user testing
fresh_mastery_check.complete_case: A new fictional Northstar card supplies purpose N1, constraint N2, two observations N3–N4, and an unsuccessful first revision N5. No outside facts are needed or permitted.
fresh_mastery_check.task: Use move from a labelled user need to a design choice, then to an observable access check; preference alone is not evidence. Produce two evidence-linked claims, one revised decision or design, an observable pass condition, and one limitation.
fresh_mastery_check.evidence_requirements: Submit the label-to-claim map, the revised artifact or decision, expected-versus-observed check evidence, and the limitation. Do not reuse the worked model wording.

test_or_check_criteria: The solution is complete and correct with no scaffold, prompt, or worked example in view.
Expected results were stated first, then at least two cases including a boundary case were run with actual against expected shown.
The written explanation is self-contained enough for a reader unfamiliar with the topic to follow each decision.
The submission is the student's own work; assistance did not produce any graded part of it.
No real credential, real personal data, or live external system appears anywhere.

presentation_and_privacy.sandbox_and_credentials_note: Everything in this task runs in a sandbox or on paper. Never use a real password, passphrase, API key, account credential, access token, precise home location, or any real person's identifiable information — invent fictional values instead. Do not sign into, probe, scan, stress, or attempt access to any live, production, school, or third-party system, and do not bypass a filter, licence, access control, or terms of service. Any practice login used in an example must be obviously invented — a silly made-up name paired with a nonsense multi-word phrase — and must never be anything you or anyone in your family actually uses somewhere real. If a task seems to need something real, substitute a made-up stand-in and note the substitution.

copyright_and_authorship: The graded submission must be your own authorship. A parent, tutor, or AI tool may explain an idea, demonstrate a technique, or give feedback on a draft, but must not produce, write, debug, or make any part of the work that is scored. Any code, asset, or text you did not write must be openly licensed or supplied for this task, and must be cited in a comment or note naming where it came from and what you changed.
accessibility_options: Provide readable text plus optional audio or read-aloud support; no voice feature is required.
Chunk directions into one action at a time and show a worked example or model.
Allow typed, handwritten, spoken, drawn, manipulatives-based, or demonstrated responses when the standard permits.
Offer reduced-copying, extended-time, hidden-timer, movement-break, and low-distraction options.
Use captions, alt text, high-contrast print, keyboard access, and text-only fallbacks for media.
Preserve the learning target while adjusting quantity, pacing, representation, or response mode.
task_accessibility_provisions: Provide a screen-reader-compatible editor, adjustable font size and contrast, and a complete keyboard-only workflow. An offline paper-and-trace route is available for every task here and is scored identically to an on-screen one.
Breaks, extended time, a hidden timer, reduced copying, and a low-distraction setting are available on request and never reduce the score.
safety_and_privacy_rules: Allow a pause, break, or alternate response mode without treating it as failure.
Never require a real password, private message, precise location, account credential, or identifiable image.
Use approved sites and tools; do not bypass filters, access controls, licensing, or terms of service.
Treat AI output as a draft to verify, not as an authority or a substitute for learner work.

media.suggestion: Optional diagram, map, worked example, source image, demonstration, or short clip supporting user testing.
media.fallback: Provide the same information as readable steps, alt text, transcript, tactile/concrete model, or teacher demonstration.

remediation: Reteaching for user testing follows the signal actually observed, not a fixed script. If the signal is "prerequisite gap": Return to the smallest prerequisite needed for user testing, model it with a concrete or text-only representation, then retry one fresh item. If the signal is "procedure without understanding": Ask the learner to explain or represent why the process for user testing works before continuing. If the signal is "correct but low confidence": Confirm the reasoning specifically, offer one varied example of user testing, and avoid unnecessary remediation. If the signal is "repeated error pattern": Name the observable pattern neutrally, contrast it with a worked example, and schedule a short same-day or next-session review. If the signal is "mastery evidence": Require accurate independent application plus explanation on a later or different occasion before marking user testing mastered. Re-check with one fresh item of the same kind before moving on, and record which signal was seen so the pattern is visible across the unit rather than treated as a one-off.
extension: Apply user testing under a new constraint, compare two approaches or perspectives, or teach the idea with an original example without completing another learner’s graded work. Treat this as optional depth on user testing rather than extra volume: one harder case done well beats three more of the same. Extension work stays inside the same sandbox rules — no real credentials and no live external systems. Extension work is never required to reach mastery and must not be assigned as a penalty.
